defects: Frames 5 and 6 are nearly the same wide shot. The last ~3 s barely change (per-second change 4.8, 2.4, 1.4), so the end is dead air and not a settle.
Mid-dive frame (frame 2) is mostly flat black, unlit chamber shapes on a brown field. It is a waiting frame with no subject and no light.
The 'then read aloud' line is caught half-drawn and illegible in a pair frame, a generic per-glyph wipe that does not belong to the burrow material.
The pairs show the camera moving at near-constant speed between keys, with little ease into the reveals. Chambers light up without anticipation or follow-through.
The grain overlay is uniform and heavy across flat vector fills, with a slightly noisy edge on the glow at 100%. It does not respond to light, so it reads as a filter on top.
The house and moon in the opening are small and pushed to the edges, and they shrink to tiny icons in the end-frame lockup. The brand mark 'Burrow' crowds the moon and telescope.
The music starts with plucked, sparse notes up to ~3.8 s, then turns into a steady wash. Above ~4 s the transients are evenly spaced and do not clearly line up with chamber reveals or text beats.
gaps: Choreography: one continuous push-in/pull-back with linear-feeling camera travel. Top studio work would give the descent weight (gravity on the tunnel, a snap when the chamber ignites) and stagger the network lighting so it spreads like a story being told, not appearing all at once.

Arc and ending: the peak at ~11-13 s releases into a held wide shot that idles for ~4 s. The payoff needs one last beat, such as a new chamber lighting for tonight's story or the house window going dark, so the end settles on purpose.

Sound: after a plucked opening the score turns into an undifferentiated pad with little sound design (no dirt, tunnel or ignition foley). Hits are not clearly locked to picture, and the dynamics are flat from 5 to 18 s.
